knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper proposes a dark-state metasurface concept to enhance terahertz generation efficiency by eliminating linear radiation damping. It combines a resonant dark-state metasurface with specific spatial symmetry to enable destructive interference of linear moments while maintaining nonlinear radiation. Numerical simulations show a second-order nonlinear susceptibility of ~10^-11 m/V, representing a one-order improvement over previous split-ring resonator metasurfaces.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text identifies dissipative and radiative damping from linear scattering as the primary obstacles limiting nonlinear conversion efficiency in metasurfaces. It proposes a dark-mode-assisted perfect absorbing metasurface that uses a low-loss dielectric dark element to enhance local fields while eliminating linear radiative damping. This design aims to achieve THz emission efficiency approximately two orders of magnitude higher than conventional split-ring resonator metasurfaces.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The proposed metasurface THz emitter utilizes a low-loss dielectric dark state to concentrate electromagnetic energy and achieve high Q-factor local field enhancement. The design consists of two gold split-ring resonators (SRRs) on a silicon slab with metal walls, operating at a wavelength of approximately 1.5 micrometers. The SRRs couple the incident pump radiation to the dark state via electric and magnetic effective surface susceptibilities.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The high-quality-factor TE2,0 dark mode of the silicon slab creates strong local field enhancement around the split-ring resonators (SRRs), while metal walls positioned at field minima ensure energy dissipation in the SRRs. The SRRs exhibit opposite linear dipole moments that cancel in the far field, eliminating linear radiation damping, while their second-order nonlinear responses add constructively to enhance terahertz emission. This mechanism is modeled using a hydrodynamic approach where the convection term drives the second-order nonlinearity.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study details the simulation parameters for a terahertz emitter, including a 140 fs pump pulse with a peak amplitude of 2 x 10^7 V/m. The proposed design achieves a terahertz emission power enhancement of over 120-fold compared to a traditional split-ring resonator metasurface. The generated terahertz signal is polarized along the x-axis and exhibits a spectral peak at 2/tau with a bandwidth of approximately 2.31/tau.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study evaluates the effective nonlinear susceptibility of a proposed dark-state metasurface against a traditional split-ring resonator (SRR) metasurface. The proposed design achieves a susceptibility approximately one order of magnitude higher, leading to a predicted two-order enhancement in terahertz emission. The authors note that while the theoretical model simplifies experimental variables, the design concept is generalizable to other nonlinear processes.

attributes.experimental_performance: about the same order of THz generation as a 0.2 mm-thick ZnTe crystal
